outcome: Mitochondrial function (oxygen consumption, basal respiration, non-ATP-linked respiration, maximal capacity, spare capacity)
Adult pulmonary function (lung function, airflow obstruction)
cohort: The study included young adults born moderately to extremely preterm and age-matched term-born adults.
finding: Adult survivors of preterm birth exhibited increased mitochondrial oxygen consumption at baseline, particularly basal and non-ATP-linked respiration, higher maximal and spare capacities, and lower lung function compared to term-born adults.
